records.public_safe_text: on tuesday, september 14, 2021 i, officer (ofc.) h. selsky #[school facility] resource officer (sro) [school facility] (vrhs). police responded to [roadway] [roadway] in reference to an automobile versus pedestrian style collision. upon arrival i met with the two witnesses, the pedestrian, and the driver, [school facility] nurse was also on-scene and assessed the pedestrian prior to williamson county emergency medical services (ems) arriving. the pedestrian was alert and conscious and had apparent bleeding on his knees. i spoke with witness #1, a witness to the incident, who advised that she was stopped in traffic traveling west bound exiting vrhs. witness #1 advised that she saw a teenage boy on her right side dart through the car that was ahead of her. witness #1 advised there was a larger vehicle to her left and she lost sight of the boy for a split second, and then saw him again as the east bound vehicle hit him. witness #1 advised the boy flew in the air and did a ""fall flip"" and land on his head. witness advised that she stopped her vehicle prepared to preform cpr; however, the boy popped back up and was saying, ""he was fine"". witness #1 advised the driver of the unit #1 was out of her vehicle, very upset and was telling the boy that she was sorry. witness #1 advised that the boy kept reassuring her that, ""he was ok and it was his fault"". i spoke to witness #2 to the incident, who advised that she was stopped about 5-cars from the [roadway], west bound exiting vrhs. witness #2 advised that she was looking in her left sideview mirror and saw the pedestrians head/shoulders above the vehicle behind her as he ran and then was violently flipped in the air as he made contact with the honda pilot suv. witness #2 advised she parked her car and ran to him and discovered that he was already up and he and the driver of the honda pilot were hugging each other. witness #2 advised that the pedestrian kept saying it was his fault, i ran out in front of her. witness #2 advised she told the pedestrian that it was ok and that it was an accident. the pedestrian was evaluated by williamson county ems and at the request of his mother, [roadway]. david's round rock by medic 26.

records.deidentified_narrative: police responded to the listed location for a major accident. upon arrival, i spoke to pedestrian #2 who was the sister of pedestrian #1. pedestrian #2 stated, while she was exiting the listed location, she was pushing a shopping cart with pedestrian #1 on the right side. pedestrian #2 noticed unit 1 driving their direction. pedestrian #2 stated, ""i thought she was going to stop, but she just kept going and hit us."" i spoke to a witness who was an employee of the listed location. the witness was able to show me a video recording of the crash. i spoke to the driver of unit 1. unit 1 driver stated, ""i was exiting the parking lot. when i was going to [roadway], i looked for oncoming vehicles. i looked left and i looked right and it was clear. i heard my daughter un-click the seat belt from her car seat. i stopped my vehicle and turned around to fasten the seat belt. when i was ready to turn left, i looked right, but i did not look left and i proceeded to turn left."" when unit 1 proceeded to turn left, she struck the shopping cart on the left side. pedestrian 2 took a step back, but pedestrian 1 stayed on the right side of the shopping basket. after unit 1 hit the shopping cart, the shopping cart hit pedestrian 1. i was able to confirm the events with the surveillance video from the witness. i contacted tid and updated a. stautzenberger #2506 that there were no life threatening injuries [medical facility]. i also updated sgt. yzaguirre #3074 of he crash details.

[person] he attempted to avoid the male but struck him with his motor vehicle. [person] he exited his motor vehicle to help the male. per [person], the male was observed to have a strong odor of alcoholic beverage coming from his person. [person] advised to stay at the scene until further notice. upon my observations, [roadway] lights were observed to be illuminated in the surrounding area. deputy d. landry, unit 43f36, made the scene at [medical facility] downtown and was advised by medical staff the male was in stable conditions with non-life threatening injuries. the male was identified by name and date of birth as juan vazquez (dob [date]). sergeant l, fairchild, unit 43s34, was advised of [person]`s condition. a case card was provided to both parties. no further information. end of report.

records.deidentified_narrative: on [date] while working unformed patrol, police responded to vision4less ([roadway]) in reference to the rp getting hit by a vehicle in the parking lot. the rp was later identified as lauryn forkins (wf [date] [phone]). i arrived on scene and met with the rp. she advised that her child, grandmother, and her were walking across the parking lot just in front of vision4less when a vehicle bumped the rp in the arm. the rps child was ensley forkins (wf [date]) and her grandmother was mary newberg (wf [date] [phone]). the rp advised that the three of them were holding hands with ensley in the middle. the rp advised that when she was bumped by the vehicle, the vehicle started arguing with newberg then left the scene. the rp had a tag, and the vehicle came back to a 2014 gmc (tx [identifier]). the rp advised that a white female was driving. the vehicles registration comes back to ashley jackson that shows an address of 90 [roadway], texarkana, texas. it is unknown if that was the driver of the vehicle at the time of this incident. i believe there were cameras at vision4less, but due to call load i was unable to check with them or any other surrounding business. this incident occurred on [date] around 1:36 pm. originally dispatch advised that the rp was not hurt but after i arrived on scene she advised that she had a tingle in . the rp advised that she wished to press charges. after this crash was assigned to the traffic investigation unit surveillance footage was obtained from target. after reviewing the footage it is unclear if any contact was made between the car and the pedestrian who was not crossing in a crosswalk. you can see there was an exchange of words between one of the pedestrians and the vehicle and the pedestrians continue across in front of the vehicle. this does not appear to be a hit & run situation.
